text:
maria: Heads-up — scheduling a rolling maintenance tonight 00:30–03:30 UTC for the saturn-edge pool. We'll do staggered node drains + NIC microcode + kernel NIC patch. Expect ~12-18 GPUs offline at peak (cohorts of ~8 nodes every 10m). kv-cache seeding after each cohort to avoid cold-start tails.
ajay: Which AZs/racks are in the first cohorts? any APAC impact?
maria: Start cohort order: az3-rackA -> az3-rackB -> az1-rackC; apac small impact at the beginning window (00:30 UTC is evening APAC). If APAC spike, we can shift the order.
sam: Can we move to 01:30–04:30 UTC? APAC customers have a spike around 01:00 UTC today.
maria: I'm open to shifting by 30m but want to keep the 3h runway for backfills. Proposed compromise: 01:00–04:00 UTC. Anyone strongly against?
leo: 01:00 works for me. Note: we'll need extra burst capacity for ~90m while backfill finishes — cost estimate ~$1.8k for the pool (GPU cloud bursts + preemptible uplift).
ajay: Can you add the cost tag to the maintenance ticket and cc finance?
maria: done — ticket <https://go/ops/maintenance/1832|ops/maintenance-1832> (cost: $1.8k est).
ops-bot: Maintenance created by maria — ID: 1832 — scheduled 2026-03-21 01:00 UTC — <https://go/ops/maintenance/1832|view>.
leo: KV-cache seeding — what's the plan/command? how long per node?
maria: kv-seed plan: after drain completes on node, run `kv-seed --pool=saturn-edge --node=$NODE --batch=1200 --concurrency=8`. Expect ~4–6min per node to reach steady hit rates depending on model footprints. We'll parallelize within a rack.
ajay: If kv-seed fails for a node, do we abort the cohort?
maria: No abort. If seeding fails we mark node degraded, continue with next cohorts. We'll rely on smart-routing to fall back to warm variants; SLA hit window net effect should be small (p50 unaffected, p95 + 50–150ms for affected tenants).
srebot: FYI — routing policy will automatically route to quantized-compat variants when node pool capacity < 70%.
leo: That fallback increases per-token cost by ~1.25x per estimate. Add to cost note.
maria: noted. Added to ticket.
ajay: Are we doing a canary cohort first?
maria: Yes — first cohort is a 2-node canary in az3-rackA. Steps: 1) `drain-node node-321` 2) wait for evacuations 3) reboot 4) kv-seed 5) verify latency + tail error rates on metric-dashboard. If canary stable for 10m -> continue.
leo: Example quick logs from recent dry-run: 
```
node-321: drain started
node-321: tasks evacuated 18/18
node-321: rebooted (bios nvlink patch)
node-321: kv-seed succeeded (hitrate 78%)
```
maria: Runbook snippet for oncall: `./maintenance-runbook --id=1832` includes rollback steps (re-enable node if evacs fail, revert kernel, skip firmware).
oncall_night: I'll take oncall ownership tonight and run the canary. Ping me 15m before start. :thumbsup:
ajay: We should notify top 10 tenants and docs with a short blurb — @product? (cc finance for cost).
maria: Sending comms draft to #customer-success in 30m.
sam: One more ask — ensure autoscaler constraints allow immediate backfill (min nodes threshold). I don't want slow scale-up to throttle requests.
maria: Good call. I'll set autoscaler override for the window and pre-warm 2 standby nodes per AZ before start. Command: `asg override --pool=saturn-edge --min=95%` (temporary).
leo: After maintenance, we'll run a 30m observation window and then remove overrides.
maria: TL;DR — schedule 01:00–04:00 UTC, canary first (2 nodes), cohorts every 10m, kv-seed post-drain, expected offline GPUs 12-18, estimated extra cost ~$1.8k, fallback to quantized variants may increase token cost ~1.25x. Any final objections?
ajay: None from infra. :+1:
oncall_night: I'll post runbook start message and timeline in #eng-infra 10m before.
srebot: Reminder — open SLO watch ticket if p95 > baseline +200ms during window.
maria: Thanks all — I'll update the ticket with final window and comms link. :wave:
